boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Ohio Northern traditions, from orientation rituals to long-running campus events.

cards.title: Sign and Paint the Spirit Rock
cards.subtitle: Between Heterick Memorial Library and McIntosh Center
cards.notes: See the rock during orientation, then reserve an approved painting slot with your group for a campus event or organization.
cards.short_summary: New Polar Bears sign it, while campus groups use it to mark events and show spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU identifies signing the Spirit Rock as a new-student activity and describes painting it as a tradition supporting events, clubs, and organizations.
cards.access_notes: Painting requires an approved reservation; visit during public orientation or campus events.

cards.title: Welcome Spring with the Festival of Colors
cards.subtitle: Ohio Northern University, Ada, Ohio
cards.notes: Watch ONU event listings in spring and join only as directed; wear clothes suitable for colored powder and follow event guidance.
cards.short_summary: ONU marks spring’s arrival with a campus Festival of Colors based on the Hindu celebration of Holi.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU lists the Festival of Colors among its traditions and says the campus celebrates spring’s arrival with the Hindu Festival of Colors.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current event details and participation guidance with ONU before attending.

cards.title: Get Down and Dirty at Mud Volleyball
cards.subtitle: Founders Hall area, Ohio Northern University
cards.notes: Look for the fall tournament schedule and participate through its organizers; bring a change of clothes and follow staff directions.
cards.short_summary: ONU calls this annual fall tournament the unofficial start of the school year.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU describes its annual Mud Volleyball Tournament as a fall event and the unofficial start of the school year.
cards.access_notes: Participation is event-organized; follow current Residence Life and event safety instructions.

cards.title: Find the Sweetheart Benches
cards.subtitle: Campus stone benches, Ohio Northern University
cards.notes: Walk campus and read the bench inscriptions respectfully; use the benches as a quiet stop rather than treating them as props.
cards.short_summary: Stone benches around campus commemorate relationships formed among ONU Polar Bears.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU says stone benches scattered across campus commemorate Polar Bear sweethearts, who often become engaged on campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus feature; respect inscriptions and nearby pedestrian access.

cards.title: Remember ONU May Day
cards.subtitle: Ohio Northern University, Ada, Ohio
cards.notes: Use ONU’s history page to spot the archival tug-of-war image and learn how this postwar campus tradition entered the record.
cards.short_summary: May Day is a documented ONU tradition established in the post–World War II era.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU’s institutional history states that May Day was established as an ONU tradition in the post–World War II period.
cards.access_notes: This is a historical tradition; check current ONU programming for any present-day observance.

cards.title: Meet Klondike’s Century-Old Tradition
cards.subtitle: Ohio Northern University mascot tradition
cards.notes: Look for Klondike at university events and compare the current mascot with ONU’s archival images of earlier Polar Bear designs.
cards.short_summary: The Polar Bear became ONU’s official mascot in 1923; the mascot received the name Klondike in 1998.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU reports that students selected the Polar Bear as the mascot in 1923 and that the mascot was officially named Klondike in 1998.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; consult current ONU athletics or event information.

cards.title: Serve on ACE Day
cards.subtitle: Ada community and Ohio Northern University
cards.notes: Ask orientation staff about the current ACE Day assignment, then arrive prepared to complete the service activity with your group.
cards.short_summary: Incoming Polar Bears take part in an annual service-learning day connecting them with Ada organizations and residents.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU describes ACE Day as an annual service-learning program in which incoming students assist local organizations and people.
cards.access_notes: Typically coordinated through new-student programming; confirm current orientation requirements and assignment details.

cards.title: Hear the Pre-season Fight Song Practice
cards.subtitle: Football, marching band, and cheerleaders
cards.notes: Check ONU athletics and marching-band schedules for a public appearance, then support the performers from designated spectator areas.
cards.short_summary: ONU brings football players, the marching band, and cheerleaders together to practice the fight song before the season.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU calls the joint football team, marching band, and cheerleader fight-song practice a favorite pre-season tradition.
cards.access_notes: Practice access and timing can vary; verify the current schedule before making a trip.

cards.entity_name: ONU Law Oath of Professionalism and Pinning Ceremony
cards.title: Mark Law Orientation with the Pinning Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Ohio Northern University College of Law
cards.notes: If you are an incoming law student, follow College of Law orientation instructions for the oath and pinning ceremony.
cards.short_summary: Law orientation includes an oath of professionalism and a pinning ceremony that ONU describes as long-held.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU identifies the Oath of Professionalism and Pinning Ceremony during law orientation as a long-held ONU Law tradition.
cards.access_notes: Intended for new College of Law students and their orientation program.

cards.title: Catch Warm Cookie Wednesdays
cards.subtitle: ONU dining tradition
cards.notes: Check dining announcements for the current Wednesday location and timing, then stop by during normal campus dining access.
cards.short_summary: A dining employee greets students on Wednesdays with cookies fresh from the oven.
cards.evidence_claim: ONU describes Warm Cookie Wednesdays as an ONU tradition in which students are greeted with trays of warm cookies each Wednesday.
cards.access_notes: Availability and dining access may change; confirm with current ONU Dining information.
